name: Question 18
problem:
$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨ϕ\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\text{ _____ }⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ)$ parametrizes the surface defined in spherical polar coordinates as 
$ϕ=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$
What is the third component of $f?$
worked_solution:
First, we write the equation of the surface in the form $\rho =f(\theta ,ϕ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}ϕ & =\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \rho  & =\frac{ϕ}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Now, a point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface has the corresponding position vector given by

$$
f=⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩=⟨\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩.
$$

Finally, substituting $\rho =\frac{ϕ}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨\frac{ϕ}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\frac{ϕ}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\frac{ϕ}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨ϕ\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,ϕ\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $ϕ\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.$

Question 18
?

f(θ,ϕ)=⟨ϕcot⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ϕsin⁡ϕ, _____ ⟩

The vector-valued function f(θ,ϕ) parametrizes the surface defined in spherical polar coordinates as ϕ=ρsin⁡θ. What is the third component of f?

a
ϕcsc⁡θsin⁡ϕ
b
ϕcot⁡θsin⁡ϕ
c
ϕcsc⁡θcos⁡ϕ
d
ϕsec⁡θcos⁡ϕ
e
ϕtan⁡θsin⁡ϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we write the equation of the surface in the form ρ=f(θ,ϕ):

ϕ=ρsin⁡θρ=ϕsin⁡θ

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas: x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Now, a point (x,y,z) on our surface has the corresponding position vector given by

f=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ⟩.

Finally, substituting ρ=ϕsin⁡θ, we obtain

f(θ,ϕ)=⟨ϕsin⁡θ⋅cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ϕsin⁡θ⋅sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ϕsin⁡θ⋅cos⁡ϕ⟩=⟨ϕcot⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ϕsin⁡ϕ,ϕcsc⁡θcos⁡ϕ⟩.

Therefore, the third component of f is ϕcsc⁡θcos⁡ϕ.
